purpose: Submission-only reference map of official UAE sources for SADA emergency warning resilience planning.
scope_guardrails: Documentation only; not automatically loaded into runtime KB, retrieval index, vector store, prompts or reports.
Not a CAP or telecom protocol validator, and not a legal or AI cybersecurity compliance certification.
No new alert channel or change to five current simulated channels; no dispatch or personal-data sharing.
Chunk summaries are original editorial paraphrases with section anchors, not verbatim or validated indexed source-text passages.
Institutional authority for real emergency warnings requires separate official operational/legal review.

sources.name: Federal Decree by Law No. (8) of 2025 Regarding the Establishment of the Federal Authority for Ambulance and Civil Defense
sources.name_ar: المرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم (8) لسنة 2025 بشأن إنشاء الهيئة الاتحادية للإسعاف والدفاع المدني
sources.issuing_authority: United Arab Emirates — Federal Government (federal legislation)
sources.authority_role: Creates and assigns competences to the Federal Authority for Ambulance and Civil Defense; it does not make SADA an authorized warning issuer.
relevant_sections: Article 4(2) — Hazard and disaster planning in coordination with NCEMA
Article 4(5) — Public warning system in coordination with NCEMA
sources.sada_relevance: Institutional-responsibilities context for warning-system planning; SADA is a pre-event synthetic decision-support laboratory, not a public-warning authority.

chunks.summary: The decree establishes a federal authority concerned with ambulance and civil-defence responsibilities and defines its institutional position.
chunks.sada_connection: Map the real-world owner and decision-maker questions for future deployment; do not attribute operating authority to SADA.

chunks.section: Article 4(2) and 4(5) — Planning and population warning
chunks.summary: The authority has functions involving disaster planning and establishing a population warning system in coordination with the National Emergency, Crisis and Disasters Management Authority.
chunks.sada_connection: Explains why real warnings require designated institutions and coordination; SADA only models alternatives before an event.

chunks.summary: The law assigns a function related to preparing and supervising evacuation plans through coordination with competent stakeholders.
chunks.sada_connection: An actionable warning may support protective decisions, but SADA does not direct evacuations or create official plans.

verification.basis: Official federal legislation English PDF, cover and Article 2/4; Article 4 displayed in official PDF page 4.
limitations: Legal applicability, amendments and real delegation of authority require qualified official review.
English translation may not be the legally controlling text; avoid legal certification.

sources.name: National Telecom Emergency Management Plan — Strategic Guide
sources.name_ar: الخطة الوطنية لإدارة طوارئ قطاع الاتصالات — الدليل الاستراتيجي
sources.issuing_authority: Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA), now Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA), UAE
sources.authority_role: Sector-level planning and coordination for telecommunications emergency resilience; no claim that the public 2018 file is the latest operational plan.
relevant_sections: Strategic Guidance — preparedness, response, recovery and mitigation
sources.sada_relevance: Reference for resilience, continuity, dependencies and coordinated fallback planning under simulated disruption EV01, without claiming live telecom conformance.

chunks.summary: The public strategic guide treats critical telecommunications infrastructure as important to national services and emphasizes readiness, coordinated response and recovery.
chunks.sada_connection: Justifies evaluating communications loss and feasible recovery options, while all simulated delivery figures remain synthetic.

chunks.section: Strategic Guidance — Preparedness, Response, Recovery, Mitigation
chunks.summary: The guide organizes emergency management around readiness measures, response coordination, recovery planning and mitigation or exercises.
chunks.sada_connection: Map the staged SADA scenarios and before/after recovery comparison conceptually to preparedness and resilience testing.

chunks.section: Stakeholder roles; TDRA Business Resilience and Continuity overview
chunks.summary: Sector preparedness depends on coordination among regulatory bodies, licensed telecom providers and other affected organizations; the current TDRA overview describes drills and resilience efforts.
chunks.sada_connection: Highlight that SADA does not control real carriers and requires human/operational authorization for any external action.

verification.basis: TDRA-hosted publicly indexed strategic guide (2018 version 1.0) plus TDRA business-resilience overview.
limitations: TDRA states that the plan has evolved; whether the public 2018 PDF is the latest applicable edition is not confirmed.
The public strategic guide should not be represented as a verified current telecom operating procedure.

sources.name: UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031
sources.issuing_authority: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office / UAE Government
sources.authority_role: National strategic direction for AI adoption, experimentation, data and governance.
sources.published_version: Strategy for AI 2031 (official published strategy; do not infer a 2026 edition)
relevant_sections: Objective 4 — Adopt AI across customer services
Objective 7 — Data and infrastructure as an AI test-bed
Objective 8 — Strong governance and effective regulation
sources.sada_relevance: Supports responsible experimentation and governance-minded AI explanations, rather than claims that SADA is a nationally authorized or strategy-certified system.

chunks.summary: The strategy encourages practical AI adoption to improve public services and people’s lives.
chunks.sada_connection: SADA studies an emergency-communication planning use case, but does not demonstrate real public-service deployment.

chunks.summary: The strategy identifies data availability and appropriate supporting infrastructure as prerequisites for experimentation with AI.
chunks.sada_connection: Reference the controlled synthetic dataset, traceable source materials and sandbox-style demonstration; avoid claiming national readiness.

chunks.summary: The strategy recognizes governance, effective regulation and attention to possible adverse impacts as important for responsible AI progress.
chunks.sada_connection: Supports human-review gates, explicit evidence and separating AI explanation from deterministic KPIs.

verification.basis: Official UAE AI Office strategy page (search-visible official text); a published strategy PDF is separately linked.
limitations: Strategic objectives are not SADA-specific technical requirements or an endorsement.
The PDF link may be access-restricted in some clients; the official strategy webpage remains the main reference.

sources.name: The National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence
sources.name_ar: السياسة الوطنية للأمن السيبراني للذكاء الاصطناعي
sources.issuing_authority: UAE Cyber Security Council (described on the UAE Government official portal)
sources.authority_role: Government-level cybersecurity policy context for AI/ML development, operation, human oversight, infrastructure and monitoring.
sources.published_version: Official UAE Government policy page; last-updated date shown as 2026-07-02; policy edition not established
sources.sada_relevance: Defines security-review topics relevant to policy-grounded explanations and synthetic scenario controls; no security certification or penetration-test claim.

chunks.summary: The official summary discusses management of AI security risks, change control, asset security, testing and application protection.
chunks.sada_connection: Document security boundaries and the need for deployment-specific code, application and provider reviews.

chunks.summary: The policy summary calls attention to protecting AI models and data, securing inference and supporting human oversight and operational resilience.
chunks.sada_connection: Keep Qwen explanatory output separate from simulation results and require review for consequential claims.

chunks.section: Adversarial AI Attacks; AI Monitoring & Response
chunks.summary: The official summary covers hostile AI threats, monitoring, incident response, and cybersecurity reporting or investigation capabilities.
chunks.sada_connection: Record these as future assessment topics; passing unit tests alone does not prove adversarial robustness or operational incident response.

verification.basis: Official UAE Government policy overview, whose page indicates update on 2026-07-02.
limitations: Full policy PDF and clause-level applicability were not independently examined in this handoff.
Do not treat portal last-updated date as original policy publication date or compliance assessment.

sources.name: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
sources.name_ar: ميثاق تطوير واستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في دولة الإمارات
sources.issuing_authority: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
sources.authority_role: National principles for ethical, safe, privacy-conscious and inclusive AI, including human oversight.
sources.published_version: Official AI Office charter PDF, July 2024
relevant_sections: Principles 5–7 — Transparency, Human Oversight, Governance and Accountability
sources.sada_relevance: Supporting ethical reference for explainability, accessibility and keeping consequential decisions under human review, without claiming Charter compliance.

chunks.section: Principles 2–4 — Safety, Bias and Data Privacy
chunks.summary: The Charter emphasizes safe AI, inclusive treatment and privacy-aware handling of data.
chunks.sada_connection: Frame inclusive warning evaluation and data minimization as guiding principles rather than verified real-world safeguards.

chunks.section: Principles 5–7 — Transparency, Human Oversight and Accountability
chunks.summary: The Charter encourages transparent AI decisions, human judgment and responsible governance.
chunks.sada_connection: Provide an ethical rationale for source citations, review flags and keeping the planner responsible for final choices.

chunks.section: Principle 11 — AI Awareness for an Inclusive Future
chunks.summary: The Charter supports equitable access to the benefits of AI across segments of society.
chunks.sada_connection: Emphasize why accessibility differences matter in simulated emergency warning resilience; no actual population access assessment.

verification.basis: Official UAE AI Office Charter PDF (July 2024) and UAE Government explanatory page.
limitations: This Charter supplies principles, not a SADA product certification or guaranteed adherence.
